The reﬁnement of eutectic cells, the decrease of lamellar spacing, the extended solubility and the increased area fraction of cell eutectic as well as the reﬁnement of Heusler phase particles may be the main factors that are relevant to the improved strength and ductility of injection-cast alloy at RT
The increscent solubility of alloying elements in NiAl and Cr(Mo) is beneﬁcial to the room temperature strength by solution strengthening
The more NiAl–Cr(Mo) interfaces result in more dislocation network at the interface, so the strength of alloys can be enhanced accordingly

the remarkable increase in the total area of cell boundaries or phase boundaries by injection casting also induces a signiﬁcant decrease in the segregated concentration of Heusler phase per unit area of cell boundaries that is beneﬁcial to the strength improvement by particle strengthening

It can be concluded that the strengthening eﬀect from more dislocation networks and large solid solution was counteracted by the weaken effect from the weak cell boundaries and large amount of primary NiAl phases
